notes.key_messages: Candidates are advised to: • give a single response, either single word or short phrase, f or each gap in Question 1 • respond to all parts of Question 2 in the tense indicated • use simple linking words in Question 2 , f or example when giving opinions/explanations • choose the option in Question 3 which allows them to show what they know • give brief additional details in response to individual tasks in Question 3 • plan and organise answers into a coherent piece of writing, using extended sentences where possible.
notes.general_comments: Overall, c andidates found the paper accessible , but common errors resulted in some candidates not able to reach higher marks . Candidates should be careful about the influence of words in their own language. Meaning was f requently compromised when the f ollowing were replaced by a non - French word: agréable , autre , pays , pollution , quand. T o convey their ideas, candidates must use a correct subject/verb accord in an appropriate tense. It is important to copy correctly vocabulary given in the rubrics. The misspelling or incorrect gender of améliorer , difficultés , personne , problèmes environnementaux , quartier sometimes compromised communicat ion . Candidates are regularly asked to comment on advantages or disadvantages, and they should be able to recognise such tasks and adapt the rubric used , e.g. l’avantage est / les avantages sont / l’inconvénient est / les inconvénients sont. Some candidates used trop/plus instead of très . These are not synonyms and can convey a dif f erent and sometimes ambiguous meaning Candidates should be able to write correct sentences and link them where possible using structures listed in the syllabus, e.g. conjunctions ( où , qui , que , quand , lorsque , si ), verbal phrases ( après avoir/être , avant de , depuis , pour , afin de ), correct prepositional linkage of verbs. Object pronouns, strong negatives and uses of the comparative would also enhance the narrative .
